claims.text: A minor addition of Mn or another low-SFE alloying element will reduce the overall stacking-fault energy of a refractory HEA.
Lower stacking-fault energy facilitates mechanical twinning during high-strain-rate deformation.
High strain rates can promote twinning in materials that otherwise twin with difficulty.
The modified refractory HEA will develop a greater density of mechanical twins than the untreated baseline.
Mechanical twins act as barriers to dislocation motion.
Mechanical twinning provides additional deformation accommodation and can enhance ductility.
The combination of dislocation slip and twinning produces strong strain hardening under dynamic loading.
Twin-mediated strengthening and deformation accommodation can combine high strength with substantial uniform ductility.
The Mn-modified refractory HEA will have greater uniform elongation under high-strain-rate loading than the untreated baseline.
The Mn-modified refractory HEA will deform more homogeneously under high-strain-rate loading than the untreated baseline.
The modification will cause little to no reduction in dynamic compressive strength.
The modification will not reduce impact-induced energy-release capability.
The untreated refractory HEA has high dynamic strength and impact-induced energy release but limited ductility and uniform deformability.
The untreated refractory HEA deforms primarily by dislocation slip and exhibits limited mechanical twinning during dynamic loading.
The beneficial response requires a composition that promotes twinning without causing phase segregation or detrimental soft phases.
The twinning response and resulting properties may depend on loading rate and temperature.
Any precipitates present should be fine and uniformly distributed rather than phase-segregated.
A controlled comparison of baseline and Mn-modified samples under dynamic loading can test changes in twin density, ductility, strength, and energy release.
Failure to increase twin density and uniform ductility, or any reduction in dynamic strength or energy release, is defined as falsifying the hypothesis.
